newsitem.title: GERMANY: Wuertt. Versicherungs leads German film insurers.
newsitem.headline: Wuertt. Versicherungs leads German film insurers.

text.p: Wuerttembergische Versicherungsgruppe has become the leading insurer in the German film pool Deutsche Filmversicherungs-gemeinschaft (DFG) in Hamburg.

"Three companies of the Wuerttembergische group now provide 37.5 percent of our capacity," Peter-Erwin Bockelmann of the Hamburg insurance firm Burmester, Duncker & Joly, which manages the pool on behalf of the member companies, told Reuters.
Until now, Wuerttembergische had only a six percent stake. The Colonia group, which used to be the leading insurer, has reduced its involvement from 28 percent to 22.5 percent.

Smaller capacity shares are provided by Victoria, Albingia, Deutscher Lloyd, Feuersozietaet Berlin, Mannheimer and Securitas. The companies insure every risk as co-insurers according to their percentage in the pool.

DFG has a total capacity of 50 million marks. Competitors with much lower capacities are Gerling and Agrippina, which is part of the Zurich group, said Bockelmann. The largest claim recorded by DFG so far ran to 5.5 million marks, he added.
Premium income in 1996 was 10 million marks, unchanged from 1995.
"However, we carry more and higher risks for the same premium volume," said Bockelmann. "Prices have dropped by some 30 percent since early 1994."
While the pool achieved an underwriting profit of more than one million marks in 1995, it slipped into the red in 1996.
With the new major player, DFG is set for a revamp of products and services, Bockelmann said.

"One main novelty is that we started the completion bond business," said Bockelmann. This is a safeguard for financial backers of film products against the possibility that the film is not completed or suffers major delays.
